What’s new

About Nova

What’s new

Every change to Nova in plain words, newest first: the same list as the changelog file kept with Nova’s code.

YOU’RE RUNNING

Nova 0.1.0-alpha.1 d948aa0a

This is the newest version in the changelog.

60 changes have been merged since; they come with the next version.

Merged, not yet in a version

These come with the next version.

NEW
The styleguide shows a proposed vault screen, for review. The app is unchanged.
Every part of Nova now has an approval setting you can lower, so it can do things without asking. Services added later get the same settings.
The styleguide shows a proposed Approvals section in Settings, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed run list in Tasks for coding, infrastructure and network runs, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed release and rollback panel for Health, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows your state sheet as a second icon style beside the mark, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed Receipts view, for review: what Nova sent out, where and why, and what that list does not cover. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows proposed provider and model settings, for review. The app is unchanged.
A check before Nova keeps something it heard about you, ready but switched off for now. When it is on, Nova keeps only lasting things you said yourself, keeps one copy of a fact you repeat, and asks you before keeping something that contradicts what it already remembers. Memory says why such a memory is waiting. In local-first and local-only, your conversation never leaves your devices for this check.
The styleguide shows a proposed memory screen with search, confirm, correct and export, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows proposed forms for infrastructure projects and network targets, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed Messages inbox and quiet hours design, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed Home Assistant connection and control screen, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed way into Nova Computer, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed way to start and watch browser tasks and a flows library, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide shows a proposed editor for automations, for review. The app is unchanged.
The styleguide has a status icon for Nova's states: idle, listening, thinking, working, speaking, needs-you, success, paused, stopped and offline. Each state is one glowing ribbon with its own shape, and the icon morphs smoothly from one state to the next. Its preview shows every state at three sizes, with buttons to change state and a reduced-motion switch. The app itself doesn't use the icon yet.
The styleguide's intro now names Nebula as Nova's lead design.
The styleguide shows "Jarvis", a proposed second look for Nova's status: thin cyan HUD rings, arcs and tick marks, one for each of the ten states. It's there for review only. You can't pick Jarvis in Appearance yet.
Nova can check its own health more deeply on request. It checks its database for damage, its newest checkpoint against what it recorded, and whether the disk has room. It reports only plain findings, keeps nothing, and changes nothing. Health doesn't show it yet.
Health now says which build of Nova is running: its commit, whether that's the latest merged build, and when it was built (or, if Nova wasn't told, when it started).
An About page, under Settings and from the version stamp. It shows which version is running, whether a newer merged build is waiting ("redeploy pending"), and when this one started, with links to what's new and to the pipeline.
A "What's new" page that shows Nova's changelog in the app, newest first. It's the same text as the changelog file, read from it directly.
A pipeline page showing what has shipped, what's in progress and what's planned, for each area of work. It's built from Nova's own records each time you open it.
The version stamp is now a link to About. On a phone it sits at the foot of the navigation drawer.
The styleguide shows the rebuilt Nova you reacted to: the shell and chat, Settings, About with "redeploy pending", the changelog, "Where Nova stands" and the Nebula look, checked on phones, desktops and foldables (cover screen and opened). The app itself is unchanged until each screen is built.
Press Ctrl K (Cmd K on a Mac) anywhere in Nova to search and jump: any place in Nova, a conversation by its name, a Settings category (by the words you'd use, like "dark mode"), or an action such as starting a new conversation. Arrow keys pick, Enter opens, Esc closes.
CHANGED
Asking Nova to change something in your home through Home Assistant now just does it and tells you what changed. After Nova has read an email or web page, it still asks first.
Browser tasks use your saved sign-ins without asking first. Checkouts, account changes and payments are unchanged.
Deleting a secret from the vault now needs your confirmation every time, from a device allowed to approve.
The app now talks to its server through one shared client. Nothing you see changes.
The side rail takes the approved design: flat rows on the rail's own ground, a hairline over the foot. On a wide desktop it opens out: each place is an icon, its name and a quiet count (tasks that need you, things waiting, problems) on one row under a "Places" label. Narrower, it stays slim.
A search button at the top of the rail opens the command palette, so it works by touch too.
The rail's foot shows which build Nova is running: the version and the short commit (a "v" when the rail is slim), amber when a redeploy is pending.
On a phone and a foldable's cover screen, the bottom tabs are gone: a menu button at the left of the title bar opens a navigation drawer with search, every place (Home, Chat, Tasks, Memory, Automations, Skills, Activity, Health) with its count, Settings and the version stamp. Nothing is hidden under More any more. Tap outside it, press Esc or its close button to shut it.
The menu button shows a dot when a place needs you, as the tabs did.
The conversations list keeps its own button next to it in a conversation.
On a phone and a foldable's cover screen, the navigation drawer lists your four most recent conversations under "Recent", below the places. Tap one to open it. "All conversations" at the end of the list opens the full conversations list.
A "+" beside search at the top of the drawer starts a new conversation.
The title bar has one menu button: the separate conversations button is gone on a phone and a cover screen. Tablets and desktops keep it.
A new chat opens on Nova's orb and a greeting, with the message box in the middle of the screen and three suggestions under it. Tapping a suggestion fills in the box without sending. Once the conversation starts, the box moves to the bottom.
While the greeting shows, it has the only orb on screen. The orb at the top of the rail and the phone title bar come back once the conversation has messages.
A fresh conversation is titled "New chat", and the box says "Reply to Nova…" once there are messages.
Nova's finished steps in a reply fold into one line, like "2 steps · 4 s", that opens to show them. Steps that are still running, failed, waiting on you, already decided or linked to a task stay visible.
Your messages have a softer background.
A conversation that can't be opened now says so plainly.
Nebula's colours now come from Nova's state artwork: a brighter teal, violet, magenta and coral. They appear only in the orb, the status icons and state accents. Pages and cards stay dark neutral.
The "stopped" red is a true red that still meets the contrast rules everywhere it's used.
Appearance marks Nebula as "Recommended · Nova's design".
The styleguide has a page showing Nebula's surfaces with the status icons.
Nova's offline copy of the app now renews itself whenever the app changes, on every deploy and after a local edit, and only then. Browsers holding an older offline copy drop it on their next visit.
Status icons are bigger and bolder: each shape fills its tile, with richer colour and less glow.
Idle sweeps diagonally across the tile, listening is a full ring again, and stopped is a heavy red X you can read at a glance.
Changes between states take 800 ms with a soft start and finish. Idle, listening and thinking drift slowly, easing in and out, over 7 to 10 seconds instead of spinning.
Nova's orb is now the ribbon status icon everywhere it appears: at the top of the rail, in a phone's title bar, and in the middle of an empty chat. It shows what Nova is doing right now: idle, listening, thinking, working, speaking, needs you, stopped or offline.
Each task in Tasks, and in "Nova is handling", shows a small icon of its own state. A task that just finished gives a brief flourish.
With reduced motion turned on, the icons hold still.
Settings has a cleaner layout: a search box at the top of the category list (press / to jump to it), a plain list of categories, and the settings on the right, one per row with its control.
While you search, only the categories with a match stay listed, with how many matched, and the matching words are highlighted.
Choices between modes are now rows you tap anywhere on. On/off settings stay switches.
On a phone, Settings is two screens: the categories, then the one you opened, with a back row.
The pairing page shows Nova's ribbon status icon instead of the old orb, the same as the rest of the app.
Nebula is now Nova's default look. A fresh install, and anyone who never picked a design system, opens in Nebula. Orb Teal and Companion Light are still there to switch to in Settings.
The navigation rail lists every place (Chat, Tasks, Memory, Automations, Skills, Activity and Health) at every width. The "More" item and the popup it opened over the page are gone. In a short window, the list scrolls inside the rail.
A place that needs you shows its own coloured dot beside its count, as Health does when it has a problem, instead of hiding it behind a menu.
Settings has a gear icon instead of the sun-like one.
Nova has one mark everywhere: the nebula swirl with a black core, as the app icon, the large icon on an empty chat, and the small icon in the rail, title bar and task rows.
Nova's state no longer changes the mark's shape. It changes the colour, brightness and movement of the same mark: - amber when it needs you, red when it has stopped - cyan while listening - dim and still when paused - grey when offline - brighter and faster while working - a brief bright sweep when something finishes
Nova's app icon is the nebula swirl, the same shape and colours as its idle status icon, on a near-black tile. This replaces the teal ball, on your home screen and in the browser tab.
The title bar is now one quiet line: a small title, with Nova's small orb at its right end on a phone (beside the side rail, the rail keeps the orb).
The message box is now two rows: you type on top, and underneath are your privacy mode (tap it to open Settings › Privacy), the microphone and Send.
Settings › Models now flags a task that runs on a model that only fits tightly when you never agreed to that (or no longer fits at all), and says how to keep it or pick another. Nothing is changed for you.
The Interstitial Research skill's two privacy and verification checks now have a recorded result on the local Tev1 4B model. Both fell short of their bar, so they keep their safe defaults: a research search from the skill is not sent, and a borrowed claim stays "uncertain". The skill's switch stays off.
FIXED
Messages from Nova's own parts (Coding, Infrastructure, Network, Local models) that arrive during quiet hours now wait and reach you when quiet hours end. Before, they were quietly dropped. If you turn one of those parts off before then, its waiting messages are still withdrawn.
In Settings > Models, a value you type is no longer replaced when the page refreshes, so Save sends what you typed.
Editing a memory from a device that shows older words no longer silently replaces a newer correction. Nova refuses the edit and shows the newest wording.
Opening the infrastructure page, starting an infrastructure run and checking providers no longer pause Nova on computers with a long PATH.
A model server that answers but lacks the model now says "Model missing." instead of "Unreachable."
Cloud budget messages no longer send you to a Settings field that does not exist.
A deploy that Nova rolled back by itself now says it failed, instead of reporting success.
Health checks no longer pause Nova for up to a second and a half on computers with a long PATH.
In Settings > Models, an open "Installed on" list no longer closes by itself when the page refreshes.
Removing a passkey and deleting a saved browser sign-in now work. Both were always refused before.
The styleguide marks when it has finished redrawing for a design change, so its previews no longer flicker away during checks.
In a phone's navigation drawer, a screen reader now announces only one current page. When the open conversation is in Recent, that row is the current page and Chat no longer is.
A focused row in Recent, or All conversations, stays focused when the drawer refreshes.
A status icon test that sometimes failed while the success animation settled back to idle.
Nova's integrity check no longer reports "ok" when part of the check didn't finish.
On large homes, it now checks as much of the newest checkpoint as fits its limit, instead of stopping before checking any of it.
On high-resolution screens, the large status icon on an empty chat, on a phone's Home and on the pairing page had its top cut off. It now draws in full.
On a narrow screen like a foldable's cover, each Health problem now uses the full width. Before, it was squeezed into the left side beside an empty band.
"What Nova did" shows the same event once, with how many times it happened ("3 times, last 3 h ago"), instead of repeating it line after line.
Numbered steps under "What you can do" are no longer cut off at the left edge. The same fix applies to other numbered lists in Nova.
"Mark as dealt with" now sits in the problem's card, next to "Try the repair now", instead of floating beside it.
A computer set to sleep when idle no longer has services moved onto it, and a service pinned to a sleeping computer now shows as "down, wakeable" rather than just down.
On Windows, Nova now notices when a computer's wired network card isn't allowed to wake it, and says so instead of sending a wake that can't work.
The Interstitial Research skill's run record now says what really happened: research about you, or a search using words from your memory, is marked personal; the skill's own cost is counted; and when an answer says "verified" or "searched" with nothing behind it, a note under the answer says so. The skill's switch stays off.

NEW
Nova has a version: 0.1.0-alpha.1, the first of its alpha line. Ask Nova in chat which version and build it is running, and it answers from its own state, including whether a newer merged build is waiting to be deployed.
Nova's API says which build is running (version, commit, and when it was built or started) and whether it is the latest one merged, so the coming About area and footer can show "redeploy pending" instead of leaving you to wonder.
This changelog: every change that alters what Nova does now comes with a plain-language entry, and checks refuse a change that leaves its entry out.
Nova is your own agent, running on your machine: you chat with it, it remembers what you let it remember, and you can see, correct, export or forget any memory. Plain files in its home folder are the source of truth.
Setup is a short interview. After it, Nova knows your name, timezone and how you like to be spoken to, and it can tell you plainly what it is and what it is connected to.
Schedules, helpers and skills: Nova does work at set times, hands steps to helpers, and reads skills in Claude's skill format. Everything it does is a task with its evidence, which you can look back on.
The app works on your phone, tablet and computer, including folding phones and iPhones, with a calmer look, design systems you can switch live, and a living styleguide.
Your devices: pair phones and computers, keep a standby copy of the hub that can take over, move the hub to another computer, and get it back from a backup.
Other AIs and connections: OpenAI-compatible services, Claude Code, Codex and your own model command; Gmail and Home Assistant as connections; and web work in Nova's own browser that you can take over at any point.
Capture from Screenpipe, so Nova can see what you were working on, with its status and errors said in plain words.
Local models: Nova reads what each device can run, recommends models that fit with room to spare, and each device has a Models screen to plan, install and assign them.
Coding, infrastructure and networking through chat, in sealed-off workspaces on this machine (Nova Computer), handing longer coding work to Relay, and a dead-man's switch that undoes a network change that cuts you off.
A map of your computers, services and their versions, and services run and managed across your devices.
Health shows what is working, Nova's own spending limits, and a diagnostics file for getting help that leaves out your secrets and your content.
Settings in one list: bring them in from a file, take them out, or change them by asking Nova.
Checkpoints, nightly backups, a restore drill and a factory reset, so a bad change or a bad day never costs you your data.
SAFER
Anything from outside (web pages, mail, imported files, captured screen text) is screened before a model reads it, and memories from outside wait for your OK.
Keys and passwords live in a vault and are never asked for in chat; diagnostics and Nova's own answers never show them.
A paired device can't act as you; steps that can't be undone ask first, and the riskiest ones on Nova's own screen need your passkey.
Nova listens only on your machine and your private network, and web reading can't reach Nova itself or your private network.

Nova's orb is now the ribbon status icon everywhere it appears: at the top of the rail, in a phone's title bar, and in the middle of an empty chat. It shows what Nova is doing right now: idle, listening, thinking, working, speaking, needs you, stopped or offline.
Each task in Tasks, and in "Nova is handling", shows a small icon of its own state. A task that just finished gives a brief flourish.
With reduced motion turned on, the icons hold still.
Settings has a cleaner layout: a search box at the top of the category list (press / to jump to it), a plain list of categories, and the settings on the right, one per row with its control.
While you search, only the categories with a match stay listed, with how many matched, and the matching words are highlighted.
Choices between modes are now rows you tap anywhere on. On/off settings stay switches.
On a phone, Settings is two screens: the categories, then the one you opened, with a back row.
The pairing page shows Nova's ribbon status icon instead of the old orb, the same as the rest of the app.
Nebula is now Nova's default look. A fresh install, and anyone who never picked a design system, opens in Nebula. Orb Teal and Companion Light are still there to switch to in Settings.
The navigation rail lists every place (Chat, Tasks, Memory, Automations, Skills, Activity and Health) at every width. The "More" item and the popup it opened over the page are gone. In a short window, the list scrolls inside the rail.
A place that needs you shows its own coloured dot beside its count, as Health does when it has a problem, instead of hiding it behind a menu.
Settings has a gear icon instead of the sun-like one.
Nova has one mark everywhere: the nebula swirl with a black core, as the app icon, the large icon on an empty chat, and the small icon in the rail, title bar and task rows.
Nova's state no longer changes the mark's shape. It changes the colour, brightness and movement of the same mark: - amber when it needs you, red when it has stopped - cyan while listening - dim and still when paused - grey when offline - brighter and faster while working - a brief bright sweep when something finishes
Nova's app icon is the nebula swirl, the same shape and colours as its idle status icon, on a near-black tile. This replaces the teal ball, on your home screen and in the browser tab.
The title bar is now one quiet line: a small title, with Nova's small orb at its right end on a phone (beside the side rail, the rail keeps the orb).
The message box is now two rows: you type on top, and underneath are your privacy mode (tap it to open Settings › Privacy), the microphone and Send.
Settings › Models now flags a task that runs on a model that only fits tightly when you never agreed to that (or no longer fits at all), and says how to keep it or pick another. Nothing is changed for you.
The Interstitial Research skill's two privacy and verification checks now have a recorded result on the local Tev1 4B model. Both fell short of their bar, so they keep their safe defaults: a research search from the skill is not sent, and a borrowed claim stays "uncertain". The skill's switch stays off.
FIXED
Messages from Nova's own parts (Coding, Infrastructure, Network, Local models) that arrive during quiet hours now wait and reach you when quiet hours end. Before, they were quietly dropped. If you turn one of those parts off before then, its waiting messages are still withdrawn.
In Settings > Models, a value you type is no longer replaced when the page refreshes, so Save sends what you typed.
Editing a memory from a device that shows older words no longer silently replaces a newer correction. Nova refuses the edit and shows the newest wording.
Opening the infrastructure page, starting an infrastructure run and checking providers no longer pause Nova on computers with a long PATH.
A model server that answers but lacks the model now says "Model missing." instead of "Unreachable."
Cloud budget messages no longer send you to a Settings field that does not exist.
A deploy that Nova rolled back by itself now says it failed, instead of reporting success.
Health checks no longer pause Nova for up to a second and a half on computers with a long PATH.
In Settings > Models, an open "Installed on" list no longer closes by itself when the page refreshes.
Removing a passkey and deleting a saved browser sign-in now work. Both were always refused before.
The styleguide marks when it has finished redrawing for a design change, so its previews no longer flicker away during checks.
In a phone's navigation drawer, a screen reader now announces only one current page. When the open conversation is in Recent, that row is the current page and Chat no longer is.
A focused row in Recent, or All conversations, stays focused when the drawer refreshes.
A status icon test that sometimes failed while the success animation settled back to idle.
Nova's integrity check no longer reports "ok" when part of the check didn't finish.
On large homes, it now checks as much of the newest checkpoint as fits its limit, instead of stopping before checking any of it.
On high-resolution screens, the large status icon on an empty chat, on a phone's Home and on the pairing page had its top cut off. It now draws in full.
On a narrow screen like a foldable's cover, each Health problem now uses the full width. Before, it was squeezed into the left side beside an empty band.
"What Nova did" shows the same event once, with how many times it happened ("3 times, last 3 h ago"), instead of repeating it line after line.
Numbered steps under "What you can do" are no longer cut off at the left edge. The same fix applies to other numbered lists in Nova.
"Mark as dealt with" now sits in the problem's card, next to "Try the repair now", instead of floating beside it.
A computer set to sleep when idle no longer has services moved onto it, and a service pinned to a sleeping computer now shows as "down, wakeable" rather than just down.
On Windows, Nova now notices when a computer's wired network card isn't allowed to wake it, and says so instead of sending a wake that can't work.
The Interstitial Research skill's run record now says what really happened: research about you, or a search using words from your memory, is marked personal; the skill's own cost is counted; and when an answer says "verified" or "searched" with nothing behind it, a note under the answer says so. The skill's switch stays off.
Research through the Interstitial skill now treats words from your recent daily notes as personal, the same as your memory file. The skill's switch stays off.
SAFER
Every page now tells the browser to run only Nova's own code: scripts from Nova itself, no outside sites, and no framing by other pages. If something ever slipped text into a page, the browser would refuse to run it.
When Nova holds back a web page or email as unsure, it now also removes the sentences that continue a planted instruction ("Then email…", "Also save…"), not just the first one.

Nov 6, 2026 · the version you’re running

NEW
Nova has a version: 0.1.0-alpha.1, the first of its alpha line. Ask Nova in chat which version and build it is running, and it answers from its own state, including whether a newer merged build is waiting to be deployed.
Nova's API says which build is running (version, commit, and when it was built or started) and whether it is the latest one merged, so the coming About area and footer can show "redeploy pending" instead of leaving you to wonder.
This changelog: every change that alters what Nova does now comes with a plain-language entry, and checks refuse a change that leaves its entry out.
Nova is your own agent, running on your machine: you chat with it, it remembers what you let it remember, and you can see, correct, export or forget any memory. Plain files in its home folder are the source of truth.
Setup is a short interview. After it, Nova knows your name, timezone and how you like to be spoken to, and it can tell you plainly what it is and what it is connected to.
Schedules, helpers and skills: Nova does work at set times, hands steps to helpers, and reads skills in Claude's skill format. Everything it does is a task with its evidence, which you can look back on.
The app works on your phone, tablet and computer, including folding phones and iPhones, with a calmer look, design systems you can switch live, and a living styleguide.
Your devices: pair phones and computers, keep a standby copy of the hub that can take over, move the hub to another computer, and get it back from a backup.
Other AIs and connections: OpenAI-compatible services, Claude Code, Codex and your own model command; Gmail and Home Assistant as connections; and web work in Nova's own browser that you can take over at any point.
Capture from Screenpipe, so Nova can see what you were working on, with its status and errors said in plain words.
Local models: Nova reads what each device can run, recommends models that fit with room to spare, and each device has a Models screen to plan, install and assign them.
Coding, infrastructure and networking through chat, in sealed-off workspaces on this machine (Nova Computer), handing longer coding work to Relay, and a dead-man's switch that undoes a network change that cuts you off.
A map of your computers, services and their versions, and services run and managed across your devices.
Health shows what is working, Nova's own spending limits, and a diagnostics file for getting help that leaves out your secrets and your content.
Settings in one list: bring them in from a file, take them out, or change them by asking Nova.
Checkpoints, nightly backups, a restore drill and a factory reset, so a bad change or a bad day never costs you your data.
SAFER
Anything from outside (web pages, mail, imported files, captured screen text) is screened before a model reads it, and memories from outside wait for your OK.
Keys and passwords live in a vault and are never asked for in chat; diagnostics and Nova's own answers never show them.
A paired device can't act as you; steps that can't be undone ask first, and the riskiest ones on Nova's own screen need your passkey.
Nova listens only on your machine and your private network, and web reading can't reach Nova itself or your private network.
